verdict.summary: You can connect your own account in minutes, but going public with Gmail read/modify scopes needs restricted-scope verification and an annual CASA security assessment. Google says verification can take several months.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 days for setup, verification materials and demo video; more for CASA
verdict.approval_wait: Several months for restricted scopes (Google); no fixed SLA published

gates.name: Testing / unverified app
gates.unlocks: You and added test users can connect your own Gmail account through your own Google Cloud OAuth client.
limits: Unverified apps with sensitive/restricted scopes show an 'unverified app' screen and are limited to 100 new users until verified
Scopes in code must match the consent screen or users see the unverified screen
Community report only: refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing mode

gates.name: Test users / under 100 users, or Internal Workspace app
gates.unlocks: Invited test users (External) or your whole Workspace org (Internal) can use the app without Google review.
limits: External: add test users under Google Auth Platform > Audience
Internal user type skips Google review even with restricted scopes, but only for users in your own Workspace org
Unverified apps accessing Gmail data with more than 100 users worldwide are subject to Workspace admin restrictions

gates.name: Verified app (public)
gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect without the unverified screen or the 100-user cap.
limits: Restricted scopes need restricted-scope verification plus an annual CASA security assessment if data is stored or transmitted on servers
Adding a redirect URI or changing product name after verification forces re-verification
gates.time_to_reach: Several months (Google); community estimates 4-8 weeks for CASA alone

steps.title: Decide scopes and path
steps.detail: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes. gmail.send is sensitive (verification, no security assessment). gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose and mail.google.com are restricted (verification plus CASA). Labels are non-sensitive. If only your own Workspace org uses it, choose Internal and skip review.
gotchas: Composio's default scope set includes restricted https://mail.google.com/, so trim scopes in your own auth config if you can.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and configure the consent screen
steps.detail: In the Google API Console go to Google Auth platform and complete Branding, Audience and Data Access: app name, support email, user type (Internal or External), contact email, and accept the API user data policy.
gotchas: The consent screen cannot be removed once configured.

steps.title: Add scopes under Data Access
steps.detail: Add exactly the Gmail scopes your app will request. Mismatch between code scopes and consent screen scopes triggers the unverified screen.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client and set the redirect URI
steps.detail: On the Clients page, create a client of type Web application. Paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config into Authorized redirect URIs. Then put the client ID and secret into Composio.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's toolkit data shows a different default redirect than one probed; use the one in your auth config.

steps.title: Add test users and connect your own account
steps.detail: Under Audience, add your email and other testers (External type). Run an authorization through Composio and confirm the connection.
gotchas: Expect the unverified app warning screen.

steps.title: Prepare a homepage, privacy policy and verified domain
steps.detail: Host a homepage describing the app on a domain you own, link a privacy policy from it and from the consent screen, and verify the domain in Google Search Console with a project owner or editor account.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications
steps.detail: Write a justification for each sensitive/restricted scope, explaining why narrower scopes would not work. Fit it to Google's productivity-style approved use cases.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the end-to-end OAuth grant flow with the full consent screen and the exact scopes requested, and link it in the verification submission.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Submit from the Google Auth Platform with the homepage, privacy policy, justifications and video. Keep project contact emails current, as Google uses them for requirement updates.

steps.title: Wait for review and complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: For restricted scopes, Google Trust and Safety contacts you when to start the CASA assessment, the final step. A Letter of Validation is issued on pass. Google says verification may take several months.

steps.title: Maintain the app after approval
steps.detail: Plan annual re-verification. Don't add redirect URIs or rename the product without budgeting for re-verification. If you call the Gmail MCP server, mark the OAuth client 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' before Nov 11, 2026.

requirements.item: Homepage on a verified domain you own
requirements.detail: Must describe the app, not just a login page, and link the privacy policy.

requirements.item: Privacy policy URL on consent screen
requirements.detail: Also keep project contact information current.
Full OAuth flow with consent screen and exact scopes.
Explain why narrower scopes won't work.
For restricted scopes when data is stored or transmitted on servers.

scopes.effect: Restricted verification plus CASA; included in Composio's defaults.
Restricted-scope verification and security assessment if data is stored on servers.

blockers.symptom: 'Unverified app' screen or cap of 100 new users
blockers.cause: Sensitive/restricted scopes requested without verification, or code scopes differ from consent screen scopes.
blockers.fix: Match scopes to the consent screen and complete verification.

blockers.cause: Redirect URI doesn't exactly match one registered on the OAuth client.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config.

blockers.cause: New redirect URI/JS origin or product name change after verification.

blockers.symptom: Gmail MCP server rejects requests (from Nov 11, 2026)
blockers.cause: OAuth client not marked as agentic.
blockers.fix: Mark the client 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent'. REST-only apps aren't affected.

blockers.cause: Projects created on or after May 1, 2026 use new quotas; exceeding is planned to incur charges later in 2026, and quota increases will require billing.
blockers.fix: Monitor usage and enable billing if needed.

blockers.symptom: Refresh tokens expire after about 7 days
blockers.cause: Community-reported behavior for apps in Testing mode.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed auth to prototype. Its defaults include restricted https://mail.google.com/. The sources don't establish whether Composio's managed client is verified for end users, so confirm with Composio. Use your own Google Cloud client for your own branding, redirect URI and quota project, accepting the verification path above. Internal-only Workspace use skips review.

open_questions: Google publishes no fixed turnaround for OAuth verification or CASA beyond 'several months'; community 4-8 weeks is unverified.
Whether Composio's managed Google client is already verified, and its end-user capacity, is not established; confirm with Composio.
Composio's expected callback URL differs between sources (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add vs /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback); use the one shown in your auth config.
Google's 'Submitting your app for verification' page was not fetched, so exact form fields are unconfirmed.
The 7-day Testing-mode token expiry is community-sourced only.
The Gmail MCP agentic-client change applies only if you call the Gmail MCP server.
